question.problem: The first term of a geometric sequence is $32,$ and the common ratio is $-\frac{1}{2}.$  The $12$th term of this sequence is{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
The first term is ${a}_{1}=32,$ and the common ratio is $r=-\frac{1}{2},$ so we can write the formula for the $n$th term of the sequence:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}\cdot {r}^{n-1} \\  & =32\cdot {(-\frac{1}{2})}^{n-1}\end{aligned}
$$

To find the $12$th term, we can use this formula with $n=12:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & =32\cdot {(-\frac{1}{2})}^{n-1} \\ {a}_{12} & =32\cdot {(-\frac{1}{2})}^{12-1} \\  & =32\cdot {(-\frac{1}{2})}^{11} \\  & =-{2}^{5}\cdot \frac{1}{{2}^{11}} \\  & =-\frac{1}{{2}^{6}} \\  & =-\frac{1}{64}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the $12$th term is ${a}_{12}=-\frac{1}{64}.$
